A1.justification: Both complete 17-page PDFs describe the same GenSPP research. Text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and can be matched despite relocation and section renumbering.

before.justification: Sections 6–7 and Appendix C report original experiments on Toy and HateXplain, including benchmark comparisons, synthetic-skew tests and sparsity sweeps.

after.justification: Sections 6–7 and Appendix B retain the original Toy and HateXplain experimental results. Table 9 additionally reports model memory sizes.

M1.justification: Section 5 and Algorithm 1 retain the same generator search, predictor training with a frozen generator, fitness function and genetic operators. The added explanations do not document a procedural or architectural change.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Toy strings, filtered HateXplain posts and synthetic-skew scenarios. Hotel Reviews, Beer Reviews and ERASER enter v2 as discussion of excluded or possible future datasets, without new training or evaluation coverage.

E2.justification: FR, MGR, MCD and G-RAT remain the evaluated comparators in the corresponding benchmark, sparsity and skew experiments. The Toy string-matching checks are also retained. The newly cited Liu et al. (2024) method is not evaluated.

E3.justification: Table 9 adds memory size in MB as a resource-evaluation measure. Data splits, preprocessing, classification and rationale metrics, model configurations, training budgets and testing procedures otherwise remain unchanged, including the complete training-setup appendix.

E4.justification: The synthetic-skew tests, sparsity sweeps, Toy string-matching checks and HateXplain highlight-fragmentation analysis are unchanged. The memory column adds a resource measure without introducing a new ablation, robustness test or case study; the loss-landscape comparison is relocated.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five distinct seed runs and retain the same tabulated averages, variation reporting and Wilcoxon significance annotations in Tables 1–2. No run-count or statistical-estimation change is reported.

E6.justification: Existing classification and rationale scores, sparsity/skew results, runtimes and parameter counts are unchanged. Table 9 adds ten memory-size entries, including 59.2 MB for GenSPP and 122.0 MB for FR on HateXplain.

T1.justification: The new Section 8 asserts O(n) time complexity for token-level rationalization, adding a limited asymptotic complexity claim without a derivation. Equations 1–8, the disjoint-optimization formulation and the fitness-function mathematics remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about eliminating interlocking through genetic search, avoiding additional guidance or regularization, introducing the synthetic dataset and obtaining better rationale quality with comparable classification performance.

C2.justification: V1's limitations primarily concern computational overhead. V2 substantially expands discussion of dataset quality and coverage, backbone restrictions, short sequences, genetic-search scalability and sparsity–accuracy tradeoffs. It also newly discusses fixed-sparsity GenSPP optimization while citing Tables 6–7, although those tables contain only baselines.

D1.justification: The repository pointer changes from federicoruggeri/gen-spp to nlp-unibo/gen-spp, and Appendix A.4 adds an MIT-licensed code/data release statement. Existing implementation frameworks, hardware and hyperparameter disclosures remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish the repository's actual availability.

R1.justification: V2 adds references and context concerning genetic-search applications and parallelism, sparsity, alternative benchmarks and Liu et al. (2024)'s rationalization approach. These extend the discussion while retaining the original positioning against interlocking remedies. The duplicated Katoch (2021a,b) entries represent the same previously cited work.

P1.justification: Most existing prose is retained. V2 adds Discussion, separate Limitations and Acknowledgments sections, moves the computational-limitations paragraph into Discussion, and absorbs the loss-landscape appendix into the method section. Author-line, punctuation and cross-reference edits are limited.

P2.justification: Figure 1 moves from v1 Appendix A to v2 Section 5.2 with the same plots and caption. Table 9 gains a Memory (MB) column and a wider layout alongside Tables 7–8. The remaining figures and tables are retained with pagination and placement adjustments.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's mainly computational caveat, v2 provides useful dataset, architecture and short-sequence limitations, adds memory reporting and places the loss illustration beside the method. These improve transparency and accessibility. The gains are limited: experimental validation is unchanged, and the new fixed-sparsity GenSPP discussion cites baseline-only Tables 6–7, leaving that supporting reference inadequate.
